content:
Seven conversations, one answer nobody wanted to hear

In this issue

  • Private equity is forcing the timeline. Private equity buys companies that are already winning, then asks them to grow faster than the platform they run on was ever built to handle.
  • The customer on your site is not shopping. The person on a B2B site is rarely there to browse.
  • Regulated commerce moves slowly, then all at once. You could be one email away from being shut down.
  • You cannot slap AI on a heap of data. A model is only as good as the data feeding it, and most companies are feeding theirs a heap of disconnected ERP exports, spreadsheets, and PDFs.
  • Manufacturing is a human-in-the-loop industry. Manufacturing and distribution do not run on autopilot.
  • The buying experience has to carry the complexity. A complex B2B product can carry hundreds of options, and a static page of dropdowns and PDFs dumps all of that cognitive load straight onto the buyer.
  • So what does all of this add up to. Seven companies, seven industries, no shared script, one answer.
